source: NCERT Class VII, Our Pasts II, History Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526)
points: Delhi became a capital under the **Tomaras** and **Chauhans** (Prithviraj Chauhan); it grew into a great sultanate after 1206.

sub: **Mamluk / 'Slave' dynasty** (1206–1290) — Qutbuddin Aibak, Iltutmish, Raziyya, Balban.
**Tughluq** (1320–1414) — Ghiyasuddin, Muhammad bin Tughluq, Firuz Shah.
**Lodi** (1451–1526) — ended at the **First Battle of Panipat (1526)**.

sections.heading: 2. Sources and Rulers
points: Main sources: **tarikh** by authors like **Minhaj-i-Siraj** (Tabaqat-i-Nasiri) and **Ziyauddin Barani**; inscriptions and coins.
**Raziyya (1236–40)** — a rare **woman ruler**; capable but resisted by nobles because she was a woman.
The **Persian tarikh writers** advised rulers to value **birth and gender** hierarchies.

sections.heading: 3. Consolidation and Administration
points: Early Sultans relied on **bandagan** (special slaves bought for military/political service, loyal to the Sultan).
The Khaljis and Tughluqs appointed **military commanders as governors** of territories called **iqtas**; the holder = **muqti / iqtadar**.
**Muqtis** collected revenue, maintained troops, kept order — but were **transferred** to prevent them becoming independent.
**Three tax types:** on **cultivation (kharaj**, ~50% of produce), on **cattle**, and on **houses**.

sections.heading: 4. Alauddin Khalji and Muhammad bin Tughluq
points: **Alauddin Khalji:** built a large **standing army**; introduced **market price control** in Delhi; defended against **Mongol** invasions; built **Siri** fort and the **Alai Darwaza**.

**Muhammad bin Tughluq:** ambitious but failed experiments — **shifted the capital** from Delhi to **Daulatabad** (Deccan) and back; issued **'token' currency** (bronze/brass coins declared equal to silver) → widely forged → had to be withdrawn.

sections.heading: 5. Reach and Decline
points: The Sultanate expanded into the **hinterland** and the **south** (Alauddin's and Muhammad's campaigns), but distant regions often broke away.
New states rose — e.g. the **Vijayanagara** empire and **Bahmani** kingdom in the south, and **Bengal** in the east.
The Sultanate weakened after **Timur's invasion (1398)** and finally fell to **Babur in 1526**.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Five dynasties: Mamluk (Slave) → Khalji → Tughluq → Sayyid → Lodi (1206–1526).
Raziyya = first woman ruler of Delhi; Barani & Minhaj-i-Siraj wrote tarikh.
Iqta = territory assigned; holder = muqti/iqtadar (collected revenue, kept troops).
Alauddin Khalji = market/price control + standing army + Mongol defence; Alai Darwaza.
Muhammad bin Tughluq = capital shift to Daulatabad + token currency (both failed).
Sultanate ended at First Battle of Panipat, 1526 (Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi).

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Token currency** and the **Daulatabad** capital shift = **Muhammad bin Tughluq** (not Firuz Shah).
**Market/price control** = **Alauddin Khalji**.
**Iqtadar/muqti** were **transferred** frequently to stop them becoming hereditary/independent.
**Raziyya** was Sultan of Delhi — resisted mainly because she was a woman.
